articles.title: Entenda o que é objetificação sexual e como ela aparece na internet | G1
articles.standfirst: O termo ganhou repercussão após um caso em que imagens de estudantes retiradas de redes sociais foram utilizadas como ‘ranking’ de termos de teor sexual e depreciativo em Presidente Prudente (SP). 16 vítimas já foram identificadas até o momento.
articles.summary: O termo ganhou repercussão recentemente em Presidente Prudente (SP), após estudantes de uma universidade privada serem vítimas da "objetificação sexual".
articles.body:
Conceitos como red pill e misoginia crescem nos debates da internet e em discursos de ódio contra as mulheres. Outro termo ganhou repercussão recentemente em Presidente Prudente (SP), após estudantes de uma universidade privada serem vítimas de " objetificação sexual".

Isso porque i magens de estudantes retiradas de redes sociais , sem autorização, e distribuídas em um grupo fechado de aplicativo de mensagens, foram utilizadas em um “ranking” de termos de teor sexual e depreciativo. O caso foi divulgado em 21 de agosto deste ano.

Entre os comentários ofensivos e classificações, havia termos como "deliciosíssima", "comível" e "arrebentaria". No grupo de mensagens, diversos alunos faziam comentários a respeito da lista. "Tirei as lésbicas e as gordas", disse um deles.

Ao g1 , a Polícia Civil informou na quarta-feira (2) que, até o momento, 12 boletins de ocorrência foram registrados, envolvendo 16 vítimas , cujos relatos estão sendo analisados pela equipe responsável pela apuração dos fatos.

Polícia Civil investiga suposto ranking sexual com fotos de estudantes de universidade em Presidente Prudente (SP) — Foto: Redes Sociais/Reprodução

Elaine Rampazo, presidente da Comissão sobre Crimes Sexuais da Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil (OAB), descreve que a objetificação sexual ocorre quando alguém trata uma pessoa apenas como “ um mero objeto de desejo, e não como um ser humano com todas as suas capacidades e sentimentos ”.

“O ranking sexual é o maior exemplo de objetificação sexual, pois os agentes utilizaram fotos das mulheres, desconsiderando toda a humanidade delas, agindo como se elas fossem apenas objeto de desejo deles”, aponta a especialista.

Diferentemente do assédio sexual , em que o crime ocorre a partir de uma posição de hierarquia do agente causador sobre a vítima, e da sexualização , quando uma pessoa tem atributos ou atitudes ampliadas com o intuito de dar um caráter sexual àquilo que originalmente não é sexual, a objetificação desumaniza a pessoa.

“O ser humano é totalmente desconsiderado, sendo apenas um instrumento de utilidade sexual”, alerta Elaine Rampazo.

A psicóloga Isadora Zambrano reforça como a internet pode facilitar a produção e o compartilhamento de conteúdos misóginos, mesmo que tais ideias já estejam presentes na sociedade há muito tempo.

“Em grupo, esse comportamento é reforçado por um efeito de validação mútua. Além disso, o distanciamento oferecido pela tela dá a ilusão de anonimato e impunidade”, explica.

Situações assim podem ser acompanhadas por justificativas como “era só uma brincadeira” ou “todo mundo fez” pelo autor ou autores da objetificação.

“A frase ‘era só uma brincadeira’ coloca a vítima em uma posição de invalidação, pois desqualifica os sentimentos dela em relação ao desrespeito sentido e vivenciado, como se a situação não devesse ser levada a sério”, afirma a psicóloga.

Já no caso da justificativa de que “todo mundo fez”, Isadora afirma que o termo se aproveita da herança histórica e da presença estrutural da misoginia: “Pois a própria normalização desse comportamento acaba funcionando como justificativa em si mesma.”

Isadora se formou em psicologia na mesma universidade em que a situação constrangedora ocorreu. “Como ex-aluna, sei que a faculdade aborda o tema em palestras e matérias, mas isso não tem sido suficiente para minimizar esses comportamentos. É necessário ter protocolos claros que garantam punições efetivas para esse tipo de conduta.”

No entanto, até o momento, a objetificação sexual, por si só, não é considerada crime, segundo a advogada especialista Elaine Rampazo. “Porém, o que é feito com isso pode, sim, ser considerado crime.”

A presidente da Comissão sobre Crimes Sexuais da OAB afirma que, se o agente compartilha imagens não consentidas dessa pessoa e essas imagens contêm sexo, nudez, pornografia ou até caráter libidinoso, tratando-a como objeto de desejo:

➡️ O autor pode responder por crime de divulgação de sexo, nudez, pornografia, descrito no Código Penal, artigo 218-C, e ser condenado a penas que variam de um a cinco anos.

Se não houver nudez, sexo e pornografia, e as imagens da vítima forem utilizadas pelo agente com conotação sexual, para satisfazer desejos sexuais seus e/ou de terceiros sem consentimento:

➡️️ Pode configurar o crime do artigo 215-A do Código Penal, que é a importunação sexual, com penas que variam de um a cinco anos, a depender da gravidade.

“A diferença é o consentimento. Não é porque uma pessoa manda voluntariamente um 'nude' para alguém que essa pessoa pode compartilhar com terceiros”, reforça a especialista.

Além disso, Elaine Rampazo aponta que o fato de uma pessoa ter fotos na internet, para um determinado contexto, não autoriza outras a utilizá-las de modo diverso: “Principalmente, no intuito de satisfazer desejo sexual.”

Já para quem presenciar esse tipo de situação, a orientação é, em vez de compartilhar ou simplesmente ignorar, como no caso do ranking sexual sofrido pelas alunas, denunciar o fato .

“Ele deve informar a vítima e as autoridades policiais para que o crime seja adequadamente apurado. Lembrando que quem compartilha também pode sofrer as consequências”, completa.

‘Ranking’ sexual contra alunas é investigado

O caso está sendo investigado pela Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Presidente Prudente. Segundo a Polícia Civil, as diligências investigativas prosseguem com a finalidade de reunir elementos que contribuam para o completo esclarecimento do caso.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia previsão para o início das oitivas e depoimentos. As autoridades reforçaram que, por se tratar de investigação em curso, demais informações não poderão ser divulgadas neste momento, a fim de não prejudicar os trabalhos policiais.

Em nota oficial, a Universidade do Oeste Paulista (Unoeste) informou que abriu uma apuração interna prioritária para identificar os autores da lista e aplicar as punições disciplinares previstas no regimento da instituição.

“A Unoeste repudia qualquer forma de exposição, assédio, constrangimento ou desrespeito à dignidade. A instituição está acolhendo as acadêmicas envolvidas e reforça a importância de não compartilhar o conteúdo para não ampliar os danos às vítimas”, informou a universidade em nota.

articles.title: Lino Alves defende acabar com 'todas as polícias de repressão' | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato ao Senado pelo Ceará concedeu entrevista ao Bom Dia Ceará, da TV Verdes Mares, divulgada nesta sexta-feira (4).
articles.summary: Candidato ao Senado pelo Ceará concedeu entrevista ao Bom Dia Ceará, da TV Verdes Mares, divulgada nesta sexta-feira (4).
articles.body:
Lino Alves defende acabar com o pagamento da dívida pública e com 'todas as polícias de repressão' — Foto: TV Verdes Mares/Reprodução

Nome do Partido Da Causa Operária (PCO) na disputa pelo Senado no Ceará, Lino Alves defendeu como prioridade acabar com o pagamento da dívida pública da União . Entre outras propostas, o candidato propôs acabar com "todas as polícias de repressão", garantir ensino público gratuito em todos os níveis, além de instituir mudanças na escolha de membros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

Lino Alves concedeu entrevista ao Bom Dia Ceará, da TV Verdes Mares, que foi ao ar nesta sexta-feira (4). Sobre a dívida pública brasileira, o candidato afirmou que a "ditadura dos banqueiros" inviabiliza a atuação de entes do Poder Público.

"Nós queremos, primeiramente, acabar com o pagamento da dívida pública. Esse pagamento da dívida pública era a dívida externa que no governo do Fernando Henrique Cardoso transformou-se em dívida pública. Essa dívida pública, que são R$ 2,1 trilhões que nós pagamos sem comer e sem beber, (é) a ditadura dos banqueiros, e isso inviabiliza qualquer mandato de deputado, de Executivo, etc. Ou seja, nós queremos (acabar com) tudo isso", afirmou Lino.

Sobre segurança pública, Lino Alves defendeu o fim de polícias como a Militar e a Federal. O candidato também fez críticas ao STF e ao Judiciário e propôs que os ministros da Suprema Corte sejam eleitos, assim como ocorre com os membros dos Poderes Executivo e Legislativo.

"Nós queremos também acabar com a Polícia Militar, com a Polícia Federal, com todas as polícias de repressão e, principalmente, que o sistema STF (Supremo Tribunal Federal) seja votado. Que os juízes sejam votados. O Judiciário age de maneira arbitrária, não de maneira, tipo assim, 'Não, agora eu vou cumprir a lei'. Não. O Judiciário simplesmente faz leis lá no STF e os juízes de segunda instância, de primeira instância, já aproveitando, estão fazendo a mesma situação", falou o candidato.

Ao defender o ensino público gratuito em todos os níveis, Lino Alves propôs acabar com o Enem e o Prouni. "Nós queremos acabar com o Enem, com o Prouni, (para) que todo o ensino seja gratuito, do bebezinho até a universidade. Ou seja, acabar com essa história de que o filho do pobre não pode estudar. Todos vão estudar na mesma universidade. Até porque nós desejamos um governo socialista e não um governo capitalista, como alguns partidos querem".

📌 O Bom Dia Ceará entrevistou nesta semana candidatos ao Senado pelo Ceará; confira a ordem:

Quarta-feira (2): Capitão Wagner (União)

Quinta-feira (3): Alcides Fernandes (PL)

Sexta-feira (4): Entrevistas gravadas de Lino Alves (PCO), General Theophilo (NOVO), Catarina Matos (UP) e Reginaldo Ferreira (PSTU).

Lino Alves de Almeida é natural de Exu, em Pernambuco, e tem 70 anos. Ele é engenheiro de segurança e ex-funcionário do extinto Banco do Estado do Ceará (BEC), tendo participação no movimento sindical bancária. Já concorreu a vereador e prefeito de Juazeiro do Norte e a vice-governador, deputado federal e agora senador, todas as vezes pelo PSTU. Participou das eleições de 2018, 2020, 2022 e 2024, mas não foi eleito em nenhuma ocasião.

O Senado Federal é composto por 81 parlamentares. Cada estado tem três representantes. Duas das três vagas do Ceará serão renovadas este ano. Os dois senadores eleitos em outubro vão passar os próximos oito anos defendendo os interesses do Estado em Brasília e ajudando a decidir assuntos importantes para todo o país. Os senadores participam da criação e aprovação das leis e discutem temas que fazem parte da rotina dos brasileiros, como segurança, saúde, educação e emprego.

Eles também analisam mudanças na Constituição e votam a indicação de autoridades importantes, como ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal, embaixadores e a direção do Banco Central. Além disso, têm papel decisivo em questões que podem mudar os rumos do país, como julgar o presidente da República em casos de crimes de responsabilidade e aprovar operações financeiras do governo federal, dos estados e dos municípios.

articles.title: General Theophilo quer atuar para destituir ministros do STF | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata ao Senado pelo Ceará concedeu entrevista ao Bom Dia Ceará, da TV Verdes Mares, divulgada nesta sexta-feira (4).
articles.summary: Em entrevista ao Bom Dia Ceará, o candidato do Novo, General Theophilo, reafirmou compromisso com a destituição de ministros do STF e a defesa de valores conservadores.
articles.body:
General Theofilo é candidato a senador do Ceará pelo Novo, em 2026 — Foto: TV Verdes Mares/Reprodução

Candidato do Novo ao Senado no Ceará, Guilherme Theophilo disse que vai trabalhar para destituir alguns ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) . Além disso, defendeu um país livre de jogos de azar, do aborto e das drogas. O candidato concedeu entrevista ao Bom Dia Ceará, da TV Verdes Mares, que foi ao ar nesta sexta-feira (4).

Theophilo falou sobre como pretende atuar no Senado Federal, criticou o que chamou de "interferência" entre os Poderes e citou o compromisso do Partido Novo com a destituição de "alguns ministros" do STF. O impeachment de um ministro da Suprema Corte é competência privativa do Senado Federal, que pode processar e julgar esses magistrados por crimes de responsabilidade.

"Você tem o Legislativo, o Executivo e o Judiciário. Então, um não pode interferir no outro, que é o que está acontecendo agora. Nós, do Partido Novo, temos por filosofia trabalhar para destituir alguns ministros do STF. (...) Nós somos poucos, mas somos resistentes, somos valorosos, assim como foram os 300 de Esparta, os 300 de Gideão, da Bíblia, e como temos o aniversário dos 300 anos de Fortaleza. Então, esses poucos são valentes, são corajosos, são decididos e vão trabalhar para conseguir aprovar aquilo que mais interessa ao nosso estado e ao nosso país", afirmou Theophilo.

Identificado com a direita conservadora, o candidato também defendeu um país sem jogos de azar, aborto e drogas e que valorize "a família e os valores nacionais".

"Essa é a filosofia que eu tenho. É um trabalho sério, corajoso, determinado, disciplinado em prol do nosso estado, em prol do país, junto com os outros eleitos do Partido Novo, junto com toda a bancada de direita, realmente de direita e não a pseudo-direita, como nós estamos vendo no nosso Estado, para que a gente consiga um país livre de jogos de azar, livre do aborto, livre das drogas, em prol desse país que a gente pensa, valorizando a família e os valores nacionais", concluiu.

Quinta-feira (3): Alcides Fernandes (PL)

Sexta-feira (4): Entrevistas gravadas de Lino Alves (PCO), General Theophilo (NOVO), Catarina Matos (UP) e Reginaldo Ferreira (PSTU).

Guilherme Cals Theophilo Gaspar de Oliveira nasceu no Rio de Janeiro e se mudou com a família para Fortaleza quando tinha três meses de vida. É general do Exército, graduado em processamento de dados e pós-graduado em engenharia de sistemas. Exerceu funções como Comandante do 10º Grupo de Artilharia de Campanha, em Fortaleza, e Assistente do Ministro-Chefe do Gabinete de Segurança Institucional da Presidência da República, em Brasília. Foi candidato a governador do Ceará nas eleições de 2018 pelo PSDB. Assumiu a Secretaria Nacional de Segurança Pública (Senasp) no governo Bolsonaro, sob gestão do então ministro Sérgio Moro, e permaneceu no cargo até 2020.

O Senado Federal é composto por 81 parlamentares. Cada estado tem três representantes. Duas das três vagas do Ceará serão renovadas este ano. Os dois senadores eleitos em outubro vão passar os próximos oito anos defendendo os interesses do Estado em Brasília e ajudando a decidir assuntos importantes para todo o país. Os senadores participam da criação e aprovação das leis e discutem temas que fazem parte da rotina dos brasileiros, como segurança, saúde, educação e emprego.

Eles também analisam mudanças na Constituição e votam a indicação de autoridades importantes, como ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal, embaixadores e a direção do Banco Central. Além disso, têm papel decisivo em questões que podem mudar os rumos do país, como julgar o presidente da República em casos de crimes de responsabilidade e aprovar operações financeiras do governo federal, dos estados e dos municípios.

articles.title: Trump administration proposes stripping tax-exempt status from schools using race-based programs
articles.summary: The Trump administration proposed new regulations to strip the tax-exempt status of private schools if ​they offer targeted programs supporting specific racial groups.
articles.body: The Trump administration proposed new regulations on Thursday to revoke the tax-exempt status of private schools and colleges if ​they use race in admissions, scholarships or other school-administered programs, the latest effort by the federal government to root out diversity initiatives in education. The rules, proposed by the Treasury Department ‌and Internal Revenue Service, aim to end what administration officials argue is discrimination against white students in favor of students of color. "Schools rebranding race-based preferences as equitable, inclusive, or diversity-enhancing does not change their discriminatory nature," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a ​statement. The proposal follows the Supreme Court's 2023 Students for Fair Admissions decisions, which prohibited most race-conscious admissions policies at colleges and universities. DOJ OPENS PROBE INTO PRESTIGIOUS COLLEGE OVER ALLEGED DISCRIMINATION FAVORING MINORITY STUDENTS Admissions, educational policies, scholarships and loans, athletics and "every other school-administered or ​school-supported program" would be covered by the Treasury's proposal. It would apply to any program that considers race, color, or national or ethnic origin "for any purpose," including efforts to address past racial discrimination. The ​Treasury estimated that the rules ​could impact as many ⁠as 18,000 schools at all education levels and 750,000 students who could be affected because they may qualify for race-based scholarships. The proposal would not prevent private schools from having a ​religious mission, curriculum or program. Religious schools could continue to choose students ​based on religious ⁠affiliation, according to the Treasury. The Treasury also said the proposal would not prohibit schools from helping disadvantaged students using race-neutral criteria, including income, geography or first-generation status. The new proposal is subject to a public comment period and would likely spark legal challenges if ⁠adopted. The American Association of University Professors, which advocates for academic freedom and has sued the administration ​to block funding cuts in the past, said it is considering legal action against the proposal. "This is not neutral enforcement ‌of ⁠civil-rights law. It is an affirmative attempt to turn civil-rights law against the very people it was enacted to protect," AAUP President Todd Wolfson said in a statement. "For half a century, federal policy recognized that measures intended to dismantle entrenched racial exclusion are not equivalent to policies designed to preserve it." DOJ OPENS PROBE INTO HARVARD'S FINANCIAL AID FOR ALLEGED DISCRIMINATION AGAINST AMERICAN STUDENTS CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The administration has sought to eliminate ⁠diversity, equity and inclusion policies ​in K-12 schools and higher education since President Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025. In addition to DEI, the administration has targeted educational institutions across the nation for issues such as race-based admissions and scholarships and alleged antisemitism on campus. Trump has singled out Harvard University in particular for federal funding cuts, investigations ​and threats to the institution's tax-exempt status. Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: I'm Gen Z: If the GOP wants my vote, stop the speeches and fix the housing crisis
articles.summary: Republicans must use the Dallas midterm political convention next week to address housing, cost of living, and free speech to win over Gen-Z voters.
articles.body: I’m going to Dallas next week to attend the 2026 Republican Midterm Convention. I'm not going for the merch and not for the parties. I’m going because Republicans are about to get two nights of primetime television, the first midterm political convention in American history, and if we waste that stage just talking to ourselves, we will deserve a Blue Wave on Election Day, November 3. Let me say the quiet part at full volume: We are running against a Democratic Party that has stopped pretending. Democratic socialists are winning primaries, and their platform is not "more Medicaid." It is a new constitution, public ownership of the economy and the end of the United States Senate. President Trump has called members of the DSA communists, and he wasn’t being cute. If we lose Congress to that coalition, it will not be because America secretly wanted commissars. It will be because we could not look a 20-year-old like me in the eye and tell him why our side will let him buy a house, keep a paycheck, and speak without getting hurt. REPUBLICAN PARTY TO HOST HISTORIC MIDTERM CONVENTION IN DALLAS, TRUMP ANNOUNCES ON TRUTH SOCIAL Gen Z is not a lost cause. Young men already moved toward the GOP in 2024. Housing is their number-one issue, and the cost of living is the country’s number-one issue. They do not care about our process stories. They care whether this country still works for people who were not born holding a down payment. So here is what I want to hear from that stage at American Airlines Center: Highlight the wins that are real, and stop burying them under slogans. The border is not a vibe. Illegal crossings collapsed, catch-and-release is dead, and net migration went negative for the first time in half a century. Fentanyl deaths dropped more than 20 percent in a year. That is not "tough talk." That is fewer dead classmates. REPUBLICANS CAN WIN THE MIDTERMS IF THEY JUST STOP UNDERSELLING SUCCESS The Working Families Tax Cuts made the 2017 rates permanent, with no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security, Trump Accounts for kids, and a bigger Child Tax Credit. That is money that stays with a bartender, a welder or a nurse working a double. Do not assume young voters already know, because their algorithm has been feeding them the opposite story. So here is what I want to hear from the stage at the American Airlines Center next week – highlight the wins that are real, and stop burying them under slogans. School choice is expanding, hostages are coming home, and factories are being announced again. And when we remember Charlie Kirk, who was killed on a campus last September for doing the one thing Gen Z actually respects — showing up and arguing in public — it should not be a 90-second tribute and a cut to commercial. His death is the argument. If a 31-year-old can be shot for debating college kids, free speech is not a branding exercise. It is a survival issue. WHO WANTS THEIR CHILD TO BE A MILLIONAIRE? TRUMP HAS GIVEN YOU THAT CHANCE Then make promises that sound like they were written by someone who has paid rent in this decade. Promise a housing offensive that treats supply like a national emergency: Smash the zoning cartel, speed permits, and stop turning every starter home into a museum piece for people who already own one. Promise a first-time-buyer track that is not another 400-page bill named after a senator. Promise the next Congress will ban members from trading individual stocks. Young people think the game is rigged, and they are not crazy. THE AMERICAN DREAM NOW COMES WITH A ZIP CODE: HERE'S WHERE STARTER HOMES ARE STILL WITHIN REACH Promise trade schools and apprenticeships with the same intensity we give tax rates. A generation drowning in degrees and debt does not need another lecture that college is the dream. They need a path that does not require a $90,000 ticket to learn a job America actually needs. Promise energy abundance like you mean it, not as a culture-war prop but as a cost-of-living policy. Electricity, gas, groceries, and rent move together. If we cannot explain that chain on national television, we will lose affordability to people who will nationalize the grocery store and call it compassion. Promise campuses will not be permission slips for political violence, that boys are not a problem to be managed, and that we will stop importing labor to undercut the kid who stayed and showed up for work. That is the speech, not "our values" and not "the swamp": specific, measurable, and aimed at the cohort that can still flip. Democrats want this convention to look like a circus, and that is fine, because circuses draw a crowd. The question is what the crowd hears when the lights hit. Vice President JD Vance opens Wednesday, and President Trump closes Thursday. Between those two nights, the country will decide whether Republicans are a governing party with a future or a nostalgia act with better production value. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION I am tired of hearing that Gen Z is "too far gone." That is what losers say, so they don’t have to do the work. This generation is transactional, anti-incumbent, and allergic to being lied to. They voted against Trump, then they voted for him, and they will vote against us just as fast if we talk like consultants. Next week is the cleanest shot we will get before November: primetime in Dallas. If we cannot win that argument, we don’t get to blame the media, the map, or the kids. We get to blame the people who had the microphone and used it to congratulate themselves. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP See you in Dallas. Don’t blow it. articles.title: El Racing y la intrahistoria del partido de Butarque: "Convenía dejar de manosear tanto el partido”
articles.standfirst: El director de comunicación del Racing explicó en 'La Tribu' los problemas de planificación, viaje y entradas antes del partido de este sábado en Butarque
articles.summary: El director de comunicación del Racing explicó en 'La Tribu' los problemas de planificación, viaje y entradas antes del partido de este sábado en Butarque
articles.body: Roberto González, director de comunicación del Real Racing Club, pasó por La Tribu para explicar cómo ha vivido el club cántabro la semana previa al partido ante el Rayo Vallecano. Un encuentro marcado por la incertidumbre sobre el escenario, primero con Vallecas en el aire y finalmente con Butarque como sede, que ha condicionado la planificación del desplazamiento del equipo y de sus aficionados. “Al final vamos a tener que viajar en autobús”, explicó González, que detalló que el Racing no consiguió “más de 12 billetes ni desde Santander ni desde Bilbao”. El dirigente quitó dramatismo al viaje, aunque sí dejó claro el malestar por los tiempos: “No pasa nada, no nos vamos a morir, muchos viajes los hemos hecho en autobús, pero no nos parece que sea lo ideal que a falta de nueve días u ocho días nos anuncien dónde se va a jugar el partido”. González evitó entrar en el fondo del debate sobre si Vallecas estaba o no en condiciones para acoger el encuentro. “Nosotros no queremos líos con nadie, no entramos si se puede jugar en Vallecas o no”, señaló. Eso sí, reconoció que al Racing le habría gustado disputar el partido en el estadio franjirrojo por el ambiente y por la forma que tiene el club de entender el fútbol. “Desde el punto de vista filosófico nos hubiera gustado mucho más jugar en Vallecas”, afirmó. El director de comunicación del Racing explicó que en Santander entienden el fútbol “como una fiesta” y que prefieren jugar “en un campo lleno que en un campo con poca gente”. Su queja, en cualquier caso, fue de organización: “Eso hay que decidirlo antes”. El aspecto que más ha incomodado al Racing tiene que ver con sus seguidores. Según contó Roberto González, el Rayo trasladó que, por motivos operativos, no podía enviar entradas para la afición visitante. “Lo que más nos disgusta es que al final el Rayo dice que por motivos operativos no puede mandar ni una sola entrada para nuestros aficionados”, explicó. Eso obligó a muchos racinguistas a moverse por su cuenta. González relató que miembros de una peña estuvieron en Madrid “haciendo guardia en los alrededores de Vallecas” hasta que se abrió la taquilla para poder comprar todas las localidades posibles. Aun así, el club espera estar acompañado en Butarque: “Yo creo que unos cuantos cientos vamos a tener animando al equipo”. El director de comunicación del Racing también se refirió a la posibilidad de un aplazamiento, después de que el Rayo apuntara esa opción en su comunicado. González aseguró que no le consta que esa vía vaya a producirse y defendió que el escenario ya debe quedar cerrado: “Convenía dejar de manosear tanto el partido. Se va a jugar en Butarque”. A partir de ahí, quiso poner el foco en lo deportivo. González elogió al Rayo, al que definió como “un equipazo”, y recordó que incluso ante el Barcelona dejó momentos de mucho nivel. También defendió que el Racing es “un equipo muy divertido de ver” y pronosticó un partido atractivo, con dos equipos eléctricos y con pinta de ofrecer goles. La entrevista también sirvió para ampliar el foco hacia la organización de LaLiga. González no quiso “meterse mucho en casa de otro”, pero sí lamentó que los clubes conozcan a veces con muy poco margen el día, la hora o el escenario de sus partidos. “Dos meses, mes y medio, yo creo que ya dan para que las teles vean”, apuntó, antes de añadir que saberlo “nueve días antes o diez días antes” es algo que “hay que retocar”. Eso sí, el director de comunicación del Racing defendió el control económico de LaLiga desde la experiencia de su propio club. Recordó que el Racing estuvo cerca de desaparecer por gastar más de lo que ingresaba en su etapa de mayor crecimiento deportivo y fue claro: “Yo ahí estoy absolutamente a favor de lo que está haciendo LaLiga”. Su matiz llegó en la organización: hay aspectos de planificación que, a su juicio, todavía se pueden mejorar. González también habló del cierre de mercado y de la postura del Racing con sus futbolistas más importantes. El mensaje fue firme: “Los jugadores que son para nosotros estructurales no se venden”. Según explicó, el club ya no vive una situación económica agónica y eso le permite defender sus intereses con más fuerza. En el cierre de mercado, González defendió también la nueva posición de fuerza del Racing. El club ya no se ve obligado a vender por necesidad y, por eso, mantiene una línea clara con sus futbolistas importantes: quien quiera llevarse a un jugador estructural debe pagar la cláusula. Así ocurrió con Gustavo y Sergio, por quienes llegaron Olympiacos y Real Madrid, respectivamente, abonando las cantidades fijadas en sus contratos.

Roberto González, director de comunicación del Racing

articles.title: Tennessee official says Flock CEO should be hanged 'publicly for treason’ as controversial cameras face revolt
articles.summary: Joe Carr called for Flock Safety's CEO to be hanged for treason at a public meeting, igniting a national debate over automated license plate readers.
articles.body: A Tennessee county commissioner is going viral after he told a Flock Safety representative at a public meeting that the company's CEO should be hanged for treason, marking a fever-pitch surrounding personal privacy and open public hostility over the nationwide rollout of the controversial surveillance tools. "I believe that Flock right now is one of the most hated companies in America. They are one of the most corrupt companies in America," Kingsport Commissioner Joe Carr told a Flock Safety representative at an Aug. 13 work session. "Quite frankly, sir, I don't think we can make America great again without hanging your CEO publicly for treason," Carr continued. "Your company is an enemy of the American people." ‘DARTH VADER’ USES DARK SIDE TO MOCK CONTROVERSIAL SURVEILLANCE CAMERAS: 'THE EMPEROR IS A FAN OF FLOCK' His comments were quickly interrupted by the leader of the commission meeting, who interjected, saying, "Mr. Carr, we are not going to threaten violence to anybody." Speaking with Fox News Digital, Carr looked to clarify his now-viral remarks. FLOCK SAFETY CAMERAS NEED CONSTITUTIONAL GUARDRAILS BEFORE FURTHER DEPLOYMENT, TENNESSEE MAYOR ARGUES "I didn't call for lynchings, I called for due process," Carr said. "You want to try the guy first, and I don't support political random killings. I definitely don't. But at the same time, you know, the American people are angry. I felt, and I think a lot of them felt, that no elected official was really going hard enough on this. And so I wanted to be the guy to do that." Carr's criticism comes as Flock's rollout of automated license plate readers draws national scrutiny over government surveillance, data security and personal privacy. Roughly 100 municipalities have canceled or deactivated their contracts with the security company. POWERFUL CRIME-FIGHTING SURVEILLANCE GROWTH SPURS LAWMAKERS TO ISSUE WARNING: 'ORWELLIAN' "I think probably the biggest story though isn't really my comments, but people's reaction to them," Carr said. "You can go on any of the posts about it and like 99 percent of the replies are agreeing with me. And I think that's where the American people are at right now." "People have a right to go about their business without being spied on," he added. "Whether or not they're going to work or going to church, picking their kids up from school, going to football practice or whatever, they have a right to do all these things without being spied on and without having the government logging their every move." TEXAS GOV GREG ABBOTT MOVES TO CUT STATE FUNDING FOR AI-POWERED FLOCK CAMERAS AMID PRIVACY CONCERNS Within days of Carr’s comments in the work session, Sullivan County Sheriff Jeff Cassidy suspended the use of all 10 of Flock’s ALPRs in the county due to "legitimate concerns" surrounding "privacy, oversight, and government surveillance," according to a press release. Cassidy went on to ask the Sullivan County Commission to consider placing a referendum on the next local ballot "that would allow voters to decide" if the sheriff’s office can reinstate the technology. "I believe the safeguards currently in place within our agency provide clear guidelines for the proper use of this technology. If an employee abuses or misuses the technology, we will take quick and decisive action, up to and including termination or prosecution when warranted," the statement continued. Despite the sheriff’s office’s assertion that the cameras had facilitated positive, crime-fighting results within the community — including an instance in which a Flock camera assisted in locating a child predator who had escaped federal custody in a neighboring city — Carr insists their risks outweigh the benefits. THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC? "If you use this inappropriately or if it gets hacked, and it's a national security risk by a foreign actor, it could very quickly snowball and become something that outweighs all of the positives that have incurred up to that point," Carr told Fox News Digital. "Or, Heaven forbid, you get a government that starts acting totalitarian," he continued. "And then they have the infrastructure in place, and you can't really get rid of it once it's there." More than 135,000 ALPRs have been identified throughout the country, with roughly four of every five cameras belonging to Flock, according to data from DeFlock.org. Flock’s website says the company has operational cameras — which sit perched atop roadside poles — in 49 states, with each one capturing a vehicle’s characteristics and license plate number as it passes. TEENS ACCUSED OF DESTROYING FLOCK CAMERA UNTIL BATTERY EXPLODED, IGNITING FIRE NEAR HOMES: REPORT The company insists the cameras do not record continuously or utilize facial recognition technology to identify individuals in a specific car. Its website adds that customers own the data in which Flock gathers and "every search requires a documented reason and is logged for review." However, instances of police officers using the technology to track previous romantic partners have made headlines in recent months, with some concerned citizens taking matters into their own hands by covering the cameras or shooting them with guns. Last month, NPR reported that Flock cameras have been vandalized in at least 36 states throughout the country, further fueling the debate surrounding if the technology is truly welcome in the communities in which they were placed. LICENSE PLATE CAMERAS AT HOME DEPOT AND LOWE’S SPARK PRIVACY FEARS Flock did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. The company’s use of artificial intelligence continues to be a sticking point for critics of the cameras, with both Republicans and Democrats speaking out against the rollout of Flock’s technology. "I mean, this has probably been one of the most unifying things that I’ve seen in my lifetime," Carr said, adding, "It’s not really a left or right issue, because I think the one thing that people really understand innately, even if they’re not expressing it, is that they wouldn’t trust their worst enemy with the technology." The skepticism has been echoed by political leaders on both sides of the aisle. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott last week paused state funding for Flock cameras. In Florida, Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis warned against expanding a "digital AI surveillance state," and the state's Department of Transportation announced Monday that it was revoking existing permits for automated license plate readers within state highway rights-of-way. Democratic Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro also hit back against the company, announcing he would encourage a bipartisan bill for an overall ban on Flock cameras throughout the state. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We need to work together," Carr told Fox News Digital. "It doesn’t matter who’s pulling with us on this. We need to work together and make sure that our descendants aren’t spied on forever."

articles.title: Maryland sheriff torches Democrats over law he says puts illegal immigrants first
articles.summary: Sheriff Jeffrey Gahler warns Maryland's Community Trust Act could force jails to release dangerous illegal immigrants flagged by ICE back onto streets.
articles.body: A Maryland sheriff is warning that the state’s new sanctuary law could put dangerous illegal immigrants back on the streets and leave more American families mourning crimes he says could have been prevented. "It’s just a matter of time," Harford County Sheriff Jeffrey Gahler told Fox News Digital, warning that the restrictions will lead to more crime and more victims. Gahler delivered the blunt warning after testifying before a House Judiciary subcommittee about Maryland’s restrictions on cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration authorities. He is also leading 16 fellow sheriffs, representing two-thirds of the state, in a lawsuit challenging the Community Trust Act. The 40-year law enforcement veteran said his greatest fear is that the law will force correctional officers to release an illegal immigrant from jail even after U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has flagged that person as a public safety or national security threat. MARYLAND SHERIFFS SHOULD NOT BE HANDCUFFED BY RECKLESS SANCTUARY POLITICS Gahler said the law could force jail officials to release an inmate who is otherwise eligible to leave local custody instead of transferring that person directly to ICE. HUNDREDS OF JAILED ILLEGAL ALIENS RELEASED BACK ONTO BLUE-STATE STREETS DESPITE ICE DETAINERS, RECORDS SHOW "I don’t want to have to open the jail door and say, ‘Welcome back to Harford County. Go victimize. Let’s create some more victims,’" he said. "That is insane." If someone released under the law commits another crime, Gahler said responsibility would rest with the elected officials who imposed the restrictions. ANGEL MOM WARNS DEMOCRATS 'WE'RE NOT GOING TO STOP' AFTER EMOTIONAL HOUSE HEARING ON SANCTUARY POLICIES "So whose hands is it on?" he said. "The politicians." Gahler said he testified to give lawmakers a view from the front lines after years of warnings from law enforcement leaders. He accused state officials of understanding the risks but choosing politics over public safety. SPANBERGER'S ICE RESTRICTIONS DEALT MAJOR SETBACK AS JUDGE WARNS OTHER BLUE STATES "I think they understand. I think they don’t care," Gahler said. "Those who are on the side of the issue supporting criminal illegal immigration, who voted for this nonsense of ending our agreements and coming up with the Community Trust Act … they do not care." "We have a criminal-friendly legislature," he added. "It’s all pro-criminal." Gahler pointed to two families in his county whose lives were shattered by illegal immigrant killers. EXCLUSIVE: ANGEL DAD FINDS ‘NEW PURPOSE’ WITH ICE AFTER DAUGHTER’S KILLING TURNED HIS WORLD UPSIDE DOWN Rachel Morin, a 37-year-old mother of five, was raped and murdered on the Ma and Pa Trail in Bel Air in August 2023. Victor Antonio Martinez-Hernandez, an illegal immigrant from El Salvador, was convicted and sentenced to life without parole. Kayla Hamilton, a 20-year-old autistic woman, was raped and strangled inside her Aberdeen home in July 2022. Walter Javier Martinez, a suspected MS-13 member from El Salvador who entered the U.S. illegally as an unaccompanied minor, was sentenced to life in prison, with all but 70 years suspended. Gahler said neither woman should be reduced to a political talking point and accused supporters of Maryland’s immigration restrictions of failing to show genuine concern for their families. "No one called Patty Morin" after Rachel’s murder, Gahler said. He added that no one contacted Kayla’s mother, Tammy Nobles, to express condolences or promise to fight for the two Harford County victims. HOCHUL ICE POLICY ‘WRITTEN IN THE BLOOD OF VICTIMS,’ OPPONENT SAYS AS SHERIFFS SUE "I simply think that there are those in Annapolis and those in Washington who do not care," he added. "It’s politics over public safety." The Community Trust Act limits when Maryland authorities can question people about their immigration status, hold them over suspected civil violations or notify ICE that they are in custody. Gov. Wes Moore allowed the measure to become law without his signature. "Maryland will never be a sanctuary for criminals under Governor Moore," Rhyan Lake, Senior Communications Strategist for Moore, said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "In fact, since Governor Moore took office, Maryland is seeing some of the largest drops in violent crime in the country." "We will always work with the federal administration when it comes to making our communities safer, but untrained, unqualified, and unaccountable ICE agents arresting five-year-olds and ripping mothers from their families does not make anyone safer," Lake continued. "In Maryland, we’ll continue holding violent offenders accountable and protecting Marylanders’ constitutional rights and basic dignity." Gahler and the other sheriffs argue that the restrictions dismantled a safe, jail-based partnership with ICE under the federal 287(g) program. He stressed that his deputies were not conducting immigration raids or doing the work of federal agents. "We do not do ICE’s job for them," Gahler said. "We work with our federal partners. We don’t replace our federal partners." He said the program applied to people already jailed on criminal allegations and allowed ICE transfers to occur inside the secure facility instead of through potentially more dangerous arrests after their release. "Our 287(g) program identified those people who were here committing criminal offenses against our citizens and are in the country illegally," Gahler said. "Then we turned them over safely in the security and safety of our jail after they were already in custody." "Anytime we don’t have to do a raid in law enforcement, it’s safer," he added. "You have the person secured. Turn them over to ICE because ICE says they pose a threat to public safety or national security." SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW Gahler said opposition to the program has ebbed and flowed with the political climate. He noted that Harford County joined under President Barack Obama, but said Maryland critics renewed their opposition when President Donald Trump returned to the White House. "They’re doing it for purely political reasons and not public safety," Gahler said. "That’s complete nonsense." He compared Maryland with California, saying the two Democrat-led states appeared to be competing over policies he believes favor offenders over victims. "I look at Maryland and California as playing a game of tennis," Gahler said, accusing the states of "whacking the ball back and forth across the court to see who can be more idiotic." NEW YORK SHERIFFS 'MAD AS HELL' AS HOCHUL PUSHES TO BAN KEY LAW ENFORCEMENT PARTNERSHIP The sheriff also tied his fight to the approaching 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. A Maryland State Police commander on 9/11, Gahler said the tragedy exposed deadly communication gaps among law enforcement agencies, barriers he believes Maryland is now rebuilding. "The complete takeaway from 9/11 was that we didn’t communicate" effectively across local, state and federal agencies, Gahler said. Yet 25 years later, he argued, Maryland has moved dangerously far from that lesson. "The Community Trust Act … forbids us from talking to a federal law enforcement partner," he continued. "It doesn’t get any more stupid than that. When you see terrible legislation, that’s as bad as it gets." Gahler said the sheriffs will keep pressing their case in court and speaking out for victims. Unless state leaders change course, he warned, more families will join a grim and growing list. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Our job should be to stop increasing the number of angel families," Gahler said, "and stop allowing American citizens to be the victims of crime committed by people who are in our country illegally." Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.

articles.title: Trump trade chief reveals what preceded Canada walking away from 'best deal in the world'
articles.summary: Jamieson Greer says Canada walked away from a handshake deal with President Trump on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber, then demanded even more.
articles.body: President Donald Trump's top trade advisor, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, said Canada walked away from the "best deal in the world" after the nation declined to finalize a trade agreement with the U.S. nearly two weeks ago. Greer joined "Special Report" on Thursday to detail the negotiations that preceded the contentious trade fight between the U.S. and its northern neighbor. "We offered them the best deal. They looked at it square in the face and turned around," he said on "Special Report." Greer’s comments come amid a fierce trade war between the U.S. and Canada that Trump further escalated by signing an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America." TRUMP'S CANADA TARIFF FIGHT REACHES CRITICAL POINT AS HOUSE GOP SUMMONS TRADE CHIEF The trade chief said that although Trump’s trade program already gives Canada "the best deal," U.S. officials were willing to negotiate after Canadian authorities approached the administration seeking a revised agreement. "I told them what we could deliver. I said, ‘We could try to give you the best deal in the world on steel, aluminum, autos and help you out on lumber,’" Greer told Fox News. "These are things very sensitive for the Canadians, and we managed to move the levers of our government to give them that deal." FEARS OF A CANADIAN TRADE WAR ARE OVERBLOWN. SO FAR, IT’S MORE OF A SKIRMISH After Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney reached the handshake agreement, Canadian officials returned to Ottawa. Greer said he remains unsure what transpired there that ultimately prompted Canada to renege on the deal and seek additional concessions. "When they came back, they wanted more, they wanted more tariff relief. It wasn't good enough to have the best deal in the world," he told Fox News chief political anchor Bret Baier. "They wanted it to be even better… These are things we couldn't accommodate." DAVID MARCUS: CANADA SEES TRUMP TRADE WAR AS ‘LIFE AND DEATH’ WHILE AMERICANS BARELY NOTICE Canada suspended trade talks on Aug. 21. U.S. trade officials blamed the breakdown on what they described as "new demands and walk backs of other commitments by Canada" that "upended the careful balance" of the negotiations. "We were ready to do it. We gave them the best deal in the world. Did it give them everything? No. Did we have everything we wanted? No. That's how a deal works," Greer said. ‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES The trade chief said Canadian leaders appeared on television after the agreement fell apart and claimed the country had "been attacked." Greer pushed back on that characterization, arguing that the "vast majority" of Canadian goods enter the U.S. duty-free and noting that Canada, along with China, are the only countries to have retaliated against U.S. trade measures. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Since even before the second Trump term, they've limited our ability to sell dairy into Canada, and they're importing things from China," he said. "They're turning them into other goods and trying to get them duty-free across our border." Greer, who believes the Canadians were negotiating in good faith, said he has received some outreach from Canada but no formal negotiations since Aug. 21. As for what comes next, Greer said the trade deal’s future now lies "in Canada’s corner."

articles.title: Ted Cruz names ‘most powerful Democrat’ as he warns socialist rise has paralyzed bipartisanship
articles.summary: Sen. Ted Cruz claims Chuck Schumer is "truly terrified" of the extreme left, warning that progressive momentum is paralyzing bipartisan work.
articles.body: Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, believes that fear of a rising wave of progressives is paralyzing possible bipartisan work on permitting reform that would otherwise create fertile ground for collaboration. "That dynamic is dangerous right now because they are terrified of the extreme left. Finding a middle ground on ideological issues right now is … the prospects for success, particularly between now and election day, are not high," Cruz said at an energy summit hosted by Club for Growth and Arnold Ventures on Thursday. "Schumer is truly terrified right now," he added, referring to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y. Cruz’s political assessment underscores what progressive momentum in the 2026 midterms means for more establishment figures in the Democratic Party — and especially the ones already in Congress — and the policy areas that legislators may still want to address before the November midterm elections. CRUZ SAYS MAMDANI, AOC, PLATNER SHOW DEMOCRATS' LEFTWARD SHIFT: 'THAT'S WHERE THE ENERGY IS' "They’re in the middle of a revolution," Cruz said. "Their problem is that they’re very driven by their interest groups. They’re captured by their activists." His remarks came as he delivered an address at an energy affordability summit hosted by the Club for Growth, a free-market group that advocates for limited government. In particular, the event centered on permitting reform, an area where Democrats and Republicans have found some overlap. Although differences remain about just how far to scale back regulations or how far to push legislative changes, lawmakers at the event stressed that bipartisan work on cutting back red tape could meaningfully expand American access to energy projects domestically. Energy Secretary Chris Wright, noted how regulatory bodies had prevented the expansion of nuclear energy — a source of power that is uniting Republicans and Democrats as a new frontier in a space apart from fossil fuels. "We have built three new nuclear reactors in like the last 40 years. It went quickly from: we didn’t even know about the technology, to 20% of U.S. electric generation from nuclear reactors," Wright said. 100 DAY SPRINT TO THE MIDTERMS KICKS OFF AS REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS CLASH FOR CONTROL ACROSS THE COUNTRY "We created the Nuclear Regulatory Commission… in the name of safety, no malintent. But since that creation, we’ve built almost no reactors in the United States since. If it’s so uncertain and so long to permit something, it’s just not worth investing in. That’s awful! Nuclear is just an awesome energy technology." Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio., stressed that many of the discussions around reform have come down to a matter of practical details. "There's a lot of conversations going on not about who's going to fight with whom or who is going to take credit for it, but rather what is the mechanics of getting it done," Moreno said at the Club for Growth event. "When it comes to permitting reform, if we can actually pull this off, Scott, what does it mean? It means lower energy prices for all Americans, us taking better care of our environment, being good stewards for the next generation. Those are worthy goals that should unite all of us, and I'm hopeful that we can get that done," Moreno said, speaking to conservative political commentator Scott Jennings, a moderator at the event. Despite a sense of optimism among several speakers — and even from Cruz himself — Cruz warned listeners that progressives already have a very real presence inside the Capitol that casts a shadow on permitting reform and other areas. "It is not the case that every Senate Democrat is a Marxist or Islamist. What is the case is that every Senate Democrat is terrified of the Marxists and Islamists. Because that’s where the energy is in their party, that’s where the power is, that’s where the money is; it's where the young people are. I think Mamdani is the single most powerful Democrat in the country," Cruz said, referring to the socialist mayor of New York City. Since Mamdani, a self-proclaimed socialist, came to power earlier this year, a series of progressive candidates backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) have won key primary races and even toppled veteran incumbents. A few notable races include New York's socialist Darializa Avila Chevalier and her victory over incumbent Rep. Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y., the veteran chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus. Along those lines, Melat Kiros, another socialist in Colorado, unseated 30-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette, D-Colo. SCHUMER DODGES QUESTION ON WHETHER DSA BELONGS IN DEMOCRATIC PARTY With pressures like that, Cruz argued that it’s difficult to find legislators who are willing to separate themselves from progressives. He believes there isn’t leadership to push back against that progressive momentum. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Look, Schumer is known for a lot of things but acts of principle and courage are not among them," Cruz said.

articles.title: Denmark says it hopes to start deporting migrants to non-EU 'return hubs' as early as next year
articles.summary: Denmark said it hoped to begin sending rejected asylum seekers to non-European Union “return hubs” as early as 2027, ahead of a Friday meeting of five countr...
articles.body:
Denmark said it hoped to begin sending rejected asylum seekers to non-European Union "return hubs" as early as 2027, ahead of a Friday meeting of five countries leading European efforts to establish such centers outside the continent.

In June, European lawmakers voted to allow member states to set up migrant detention centers outside the EU, known as "return hubs." Any EU nation can now negotiate on its own or in small coalitions to deport migrants not to their home countries but to facilities yet to be built in third countries, outside the 27-nation bloc.

"We cannot accept that people without a legal stay continue to reside in our respective countries," Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said on Friday as he welcomed ministers from Germany, Austria, The Netherlands and Greece to Copenhagen to discuss progress on establishing the deportation centers outside Europe.

"And at the same time we would like to work together with third countries to be able to give irregular migrants a second chance in a partner country," Rasmussen said.

The five countries have been negotiating with governments mainly in Africa to host sites to hold rejected asylum seekers, pioneering the initiative for the whole of the EU.

In an interview with Danish broadcaster DR published on Friday, Denmark's Immigration and Integration Minister Morten Bødskov said he hoped that the non-EU return hubs would already be in place in 2027. Bødskov said talks with non-EU countries had reached a crucial phase.

"Today we take the next step, here today with my European colleagues, to realize return hubs as soon as possible in the upcoming years," Bart van den Brink, Austria's asylum and migration minister, said in Copenhagen.

In early August, a spokesperson for the Rwandan government told local media that "it was natural" for her government to negotiate with European countries and others to potentially host asylum seekers who are not allowed to live elsewhere.

Migrant rights group have criticized European efforts to set up deportation centers abroad where it may be difficult to monitor and enforce human rights compliance.

In an emailed statement, Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights, Michael O'Flaherty, said "vague assurances of compliance with human rights law are not enough."

"States need to commit to the guardrails necessary to prevent setting up human rights black holes," he said.

Brussels-based rights group PICUM condemned the meeting in Copenhagen.

"EU leaders may call these centers an "innovative solution," but outsourcing migration control is an old tactic to simply move people out of sight and evade human rights obligations," the group's director Michele LeVoy said.

AP journalist Philipp Jenne in Vienna and Sam McNeil in Brussels contributed to this report.

articles.title: Live updates: First mail ballots being sent amid challenge to Trump’s restrictions
articles.summary: Live updates and the latest news as the first mail ballots being sent amid challenge to Trump’s restrictions and Missouri and Maryland Democrats scored wins in state redistricting challenges.
articles.body:
What to know today FIRST BALLOTS MAILED: The first ballots of the 2026 general election are going out in the mail today even as President Donald Trump appeals a challenge to his executive order seeking to restrict mail voting to the Supreme Court. North Carolina will begin sending absentee ballots this afternoon to voters who have requested them in all 100 counties. CONGRESSIONAL MAPS: The Missouri Supreme Court ruled yesterday that the state’s redrawn congressional map, which would draw Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver out of his seat, cannot be used in this year’s elections in a blow to Republicans. Meanwhile, Maryland's Supreme Court said a Democratic redistricting amendment to the state constitution must be put on the November ballot. ARMY APPOINTMENT: Trump on Thursday named Adam Telle, a civilian leader in the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, as the acting Army secretary following the departure of Dan Driscoll amid widespread reports of tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Live updates and the latest news as the first mail ballots being sent amid challenge to Trump’s restrictions and Missouri and Maryland Democrats scored wins in state redistricting challenges.
